America’s Lame-Duck Autocrat

Ruth Ben-Ghiat

When autocrats suffer a defeat, they tend to double down, such as by intensifying repression at home or behaving more recklessly abroad. With two years left in office after historic midterm election losses, this is the road US President Donald Trump appears to be taking.

Aaron Schwartz/Getty Images

Nov 20, 2026
6 min read

NEW YORK—Like many authoritarians, US President Donald Trump cannot stand it when the spotlight is on anyone other than him. So, before this month’s midterm elections, he instructed voters to pretend it was him on the ballot. And that is what they did, though the result was not what Trump expected: Americans voted in record numbers—the second-highest turnout for a midterm election since 1914—to reject Trump’s Republican Party.
